strengths: CARVE addresses a relevant problem: improving fine-grained VLM perception without training or external localization tools. Contrasting general-prompt and question-specific attention provides a simple mechanism for selecting regions to mask, crop, and magnify.

The empirical coverage is substantial: seven benchmarks, four main backbones, and additional TextVQA results on three recent models. Reported improvements include LLaVA-1.5-7B increasing from 38.7% to 66.5% on V*, with paired significance tests supporting the gain.

The ablations examine layers, decoding steps, mask parameters, direct attention masking, and additive versus multiplicative contrast. Table 4 provides encouraging evidence for contrastive normalization on TextVQA: 82.0% versus 78.6% with direct question-attention masking.

The manuscript reports latency and memory costs and explicitly discusses failures when masking removes global spatial context. The closed-form optimization derivation is algebraically sound under the stated positivity assumptions, and the appendix appropriately qualifies its idealized nature.
weaknesses: The decomposition evidence does not establish the proposed semantic/noise interpretation. Defining Fvis as general-prompt attention makes the factorization possible by construction; it does not show that this factor represents visual noise. Likewise, measuring KL(A(G)||U) tests the observed attention distribution, not the latent assumption Fsem(G,I)≈1. The additive-versus-multiplicative comparison supports a useful heuristic but does not validate the claimed decomposition.

Attention scaling is a consequential unresolved detail. Equation 9 approximates semantic recovery only when A(G)_i is much larger than λ, yet λ=0.05 while attention is described as a probability distribution over many visual tokens. Under that normalization, at most 20 tokens can even reach 0.05. The paper needs to specify any rescaling and test sensitivity to λ; otherwise, the stated operating regime and the strength of contrastive normalization are unclear.

Core implementation details remain insufficient for reproduction: head aggregation, visual-token renormalization, token-to-pixel interpolation, and alignment of general-description and question-answer sequences with different lengths are unspecified. Main-table mask configurations and separation between tuning and evaluation samples are also unclear. Appendix B.1 specifies T=[0,5) for extended experiments, whereas Appendix G describes Tfull while reproducing the same full-method results, leaving the exact configurations ambiguous.

The empirical case does not fully isolate the contribution beyond existing attention-guided zooming. Table 5 compares ViCrop on one model and TextVQA, and Table 3 adds useful comparisons on other tasks, but V*—where the largest gains occur—has no competing-method comparison. There is also no controlled crop-and-resize-only versus masking-plus-cropping ablation using identical regions. Consequently, the specific value of pixel masking and its advantage on the headline benchmark remain uncertain. Restricting Qwen inputs to 448×448 also warrants a native-resolution or comparable-compute baseline.

Section 3 repeatedly gives causal interpretations to observational correlations. Image difficulty, target size, answer length, and attention normalization could affect both entropy and accuracy. The binned plots lack sufficient sample-count and statistical detail to establish the asserted mechanism, while two manually masked examples cannot disentangle noise suppression from magnification. The findings support association more strongly than causation.

The proposed early-termination optimization is incomplete as described. Attention from later autoregressive steps requires generating preceding tokens, ordinarily using the complete decoder and output head. Stopping both preliminary passes at an intermediate layer cannot directly produce the stated Tfull or final-token attention without an additional mechanism. This affects the claimed optimization potential rather than necessarily invalidating the measured overhead, but it should be corrected.

strengths: CARVE addresses a relevant computer-vision problem: improving fine-grained VLM perception without additional training or external segmentation models. Contrasting question-conditioned and general-description attention provides a simple, potentially useful region-selection mechanism.

The reported evaluation is broad: seven benchmarks, four main models, and additional TextVQA experiments with Qwen3-VL and Gemma-3. Some improvements are substantial, including LLaVA-1.5-7B rising from 38.7% to 66.5% on V*. Appendix H provides paired significance tests for this benchmark.

The paper includes meaningful component, layer, temporal, prompt, and masking analyses. Table 4 supports an incremental benefit from contrastive normalization on its TextVQA subset: 82.0% versus 78.6% for direct question-attention masking.

The manuscript acknowledges its dependence on spatially localized evidence, illustrates a failure involving global depth cues, and reports measured latency and memory overhead. These disclosures help delimit the method's practical scope.
weaknesses: The central semantic/noise interpretation is not established. The closed-form minimizer is correct for the stipulated objective, but defining Fvis through general-prompt attention and Fsem through a ratio does not establish that these factors represent noise and semantics. In particular, Appendix G measures KL(A(G)||U), whereas the assumption concerns the unobserved Fsem(G,I); uniformity of the product cannot independently validate uniformity of that factor. The additive comparison supports a useful heuristic, not the claimed decomposition.

Attention scaling is a consequential unresolved detail. Equation 9 approximates semantic recovery only when Fvis,i is much larger than lambda, yet lambda=0.05 and the attention maps are described as distributions over hundreds of visual tokens. For near-uniform normalized attention, typical entries are far below 0.05, so the denominator would be dominated by regularization. The paper needs to specify its actual normalization or rescaling, examine lambda sensitivity, and show whether its theoretical operating condition holds.

Section 3 overinterprets observational evidence as a causal mechanism. Binned complexity–entropy and entropy–accuracy associations do not establish that complexity impairs performance through attention dispersion; target size, question difficulty, and text density are plausible confounders. Sample counts and correlation statistics are missing. Moreover, Fig. 5(b) visibly fluctuates across deeper layers despite the text claiming a monotonic decrease. Controlled interventions are needed to support the stronger mechanism claims.

The experiments do not sufficiently isolate the contribution from cropping and increased effective resolution. Qwen models are evaluated at a fixed 448×448 resolution, making a native higher-resolution baseline particularly relevant. A matched crop-and-resize experiment with and without background masking would test the claimed value of pixel-level suppression. Direct-attention masking is a useful control, but its contrastive improvement is only 0.04 points on ChartQA and 0.20 on ScienceQA. ViCrop and SD-RPN comparisons are absent on V*, where the largest gains are reported.

Important implementation and evaluation details remain ambiguous. Algorithm 1 contrasts corresponding generation steps from two responses that can have different lengths, without specifying alignment or termination handling. Head aggregation, token-to-pixel interpolation, and the precise masking operation are insufficiently described. Appendix B.1 specifies T=[0,5) for extended experiments, while Appendix G describes Tfull for a closely related ablation. Prompt and hyperparameter selection use TextVQA subsets without clearly stating separation from evaluation examples. These omissions materially hinder reproduction.

The proposed early-termination optimization in Appendices B and C is not justified for the stated autoregressive procedure: obtaining subsequent generated tokens ordinarily requires completing the model's remaining layers and output head. No intermediate exit mechanism is provided. Measured results remain useful, but the proposed savings should not be treated as established. Table 5 also shows approximately 7.9× end-to-end latency versus vanilla inference, motivating stronger comparisons at matched computational budgets.

strengths: CARVE addresses a relevant computer-vision problem with a simple, training-free pipeline: contrast question-conditioned and general-prompt attention, then mask, crop, and enlarge relevant regions. Under Algorithms/General, this is a potentially useful practical contribution.

The empirical coverage is substantial: seven benchmarks, four principal models, and additional TextVQA experiments on Qwen3-VL and Gemma-3. Reported improvements include LLaVA-1.5-7B increasing from 38.7% to 66.5% on V*, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B improving from 54.3% to 63.0% DocVQA exact match.

The component ablation provides evidence that contrastive normalization contributes beyond direct attention masking: Table 4 reports 82.0% versus 78.6% on the TextVQA subset. Comparisons with additive contrast, layer and token selection experiments, and paired significance tests on V* further strengthen the empirical case.
The manuscript reports measured runtime and memory costs and explicitly discusses failures when masking removes global spatial context. These limitations help define the method’s useful scope.
weaknesses: The theoretical analysis establishes properties of an assumed factorization, rather than identifying semantic signal and visual noise in real attention. Defining Fvis through general-prompt attention makes the ratio decomposition possible, but does not establish that this factor represents noise. Moreover, measuring KL(A(G)||U) does not validate uniformity of the unobserved Fsem(G,I). The optimization derivation is reasonable under its assumptions, but the claimed empirical validation of those assumptions is insufficient.

Important implementation details remain unresolved: attention-head aggregation, normalization over visual tokens, alignment of differently sized general-description and answer sequences, and projection from tokens to pixels. Attention scaling is particularly consequential because lambda=0.05 may dominate typical normalized visual-token weights, whereas the semantic-recovery argument requires Fvis,i much greater than lambda. No lambda sensitivity analysis resolves this issue. Appendix B also specifies T=[0,5) for extended experiments, while Appendix G describes Tfull for related ablations; the main tables do not fully specify their masking configuration or its selection protocol.

The evaluation does not sufficiently separate improvements from recovery of detail lost through restricted input resolution. Qwen models are evaluated at 448×448, but there is no comparison with their native dynamic-resolution operation or a higher-resolution baseline under comparable compute. This matters especially for OCR, documents, and small-target recognition, where cropping and magnification are intrinsically advantageous. The strongest V* gains also lack direct comparisons with the competing refinement methods.

Section 3 overinterprets correlations as a causal mechanism. Binned complexity–entropy and entropy–accuracy relationships do not establish that texture or color complexity reduces accuracy through attention dispersion; target size, task difficulty, and answer properties could affect these relationships. Sample counts, correlation statistics, and controlled interventions are needed to substantiate the stronger mechanistic claims.

The proposed early-termination optimization is incompatible with ordinary multi-token autoregressive attention extraction as described: generating subsequent tokens generally requires completing the decoder and output head, even when attention is collected from intermediate layers. Appendix C therefore does not establish the claimed savings for Tfull without an additional generation mechanism. Measured costs remain substantial: approximately threefold GPU time, and 1.34 seconds versus 0.17 seconds end-to-end latency in Table 5.
